In my opinion, the target of the Ansarallah ballistic missile attack on Riyadh was likely King Salman Airbase, just south of Riyadh. 
If the target was Prince Sultan Airbase, there likely wouldn't have been any early warning alerts for Riyadh, as it is located 80 km from the city. Early warning alerts typically weren't triggered for Riyadh when Prince Sultan Airbase was attacked by Iran earlier this year.

🚀 Yemeni ballistic missiles over Riyadh
Footage from social media shows the skies above Riyadh and the sound of interceptions after Yemeni ballistic missiles were fired toward the Saudi capital.
The likely target was Prince Sultan Air Base, which also hosts US troops. the base is located roughly 80 km from Riyadh — meaning early warning alerts typically aren't triggered for the city when the base is attacked — the same alert pattern observed when Iran struck the same base earlier this year.
Local reports indicate significant disruptions and malfunctions in navigation systems at Riyadh International Airport.

🚨💥 Exclusive images show severe destruction at US base in Kuwait
Images obtained by MeidasTouch reveal extensive damage at a US military base in Kuwait following Iranian strikes, with multiple structures completely leveled and debris scattered across wide areas.
🔴 A hardened bunker — the exact shelter US troops are trained to run to during incoming fire — took a direct drone hit
🔴 The base's airfield was completely destroyed

Hardened shelters are the last line of defense. They're built to withstand direct hits. Troops are drilled to reach them when missiles are inbound. If a bunker takes a direct strike, the assumption that anywhere on base is safe collapses.
The US said the war was under control, but the base in Kuwait says otherwise.

events.text:
🇺🇸 🚜 US redeploying its African Reaper drone fleet as far from Iran as possible
 
AFRICOM is relinquishing “most” of its MQ-9s to SOUTHCOM – the combatant command responsible for US military operations in Latin America, sources have told CNN.
➡️The White House is reportedly planning major “counternarcotics and counterterrorism operations” in the region in places like Ecuador, and could use the drones for surveillance and strike missions.
One source said it’s still being debated whether “some” of AFRICOM’s drones may be redeployed to the Middle East instead, where [Iran](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74713) and [Yemen’s Houthis](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/74688) have been swatting down American UAVs down like flies.
The US military and CIA deployed Reaper drones against Venezuela last year, targeting a port facility and dozens of small vessels in international waters which Washington claimed were carrying narcotics (claims that were never proven). That campaign killed at least 230 people.
🤔Whether the transferred drones will actually be used for “counterterrorism and counternarcotics” or a new regime change attack (against Cuba, for example) remains unclear.
Trump has spent much of the year [threatening “military action”](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/68354) against Cuba unless Havana “makes a deal” with him, tangerine Michael Corleone-style. However, his hopes for a Venezuela 2.0 scenario may backfire, with Cuba receiving assistance from countries like Iran and Belarus over the years to ramp up its asymmetric defense capabilities.
If the campaign actually becomes about targeting drug cartels, SOUTHCOM might have a better shot of declaring ‘victory’ in a ‘splendid little war’ ahead of the midterms. But then again, why would the CIA [target its own clients](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/60875)?
